title: 9470: triple-channel scorer to an open drum path
text:
## 9470: triple-channel scorer to an open drum path

Version: 9470 engineering reference and version history. [Technical source](https://9470techbinder.vercel.app/process/)

**Published construction:** Triple shooter at early events; DCMP drum uses a full-width roller, pivoting hood rollers and three feeder rollers.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Higher ceiling without a channel-settling step.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The significant change is the removal of restrictive channel interfaces, not simply a larger launch wheel. Dividers can stabilize a piece path while creating an arch or an extra alignment delay; an open drum path can accept a broader front but needs consistent compression across its width. The early triple shooter remains an intentional schedule choice rather than a failed idea in every context. A team with an early event can rationally choose a lower ceiling that preserves practice time, then rebuild once the feed and current demands are understood.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Compare first-shot delay, sustained output and nearly-empty-hopper output across both configurations under the same supply conditions.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

title: 9470: reinforce the proven failure while preserving geometry

## 9470: reinforce the proven failure while preserving geometry

Version: 9470 engineering reference and version history. [Technical source](https://9470techbinder.vercel.app/process/)

**Published construction:** Worlds intake uses stacked quarter-inch SRP side plates with leaf-spring mounting and reinforced motor plates.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** DCMP damage made intake survival the next priority.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** Changing material without changing the mounting boundary may fail to create the intended compliance. A leaf-spring arrangement needs room to bend, a predictable load path and fasteners that do not clamp the compliant region into an unintended rigid joint. Reinforcing the motor plate addresses a concentrated load while preserving the pickup geometry that the drivers already know. This is a useful rebuild principle: once the collection and shot behavior work, the largest improvement may be a structural interface that prevents losing the entire match rather than another nominal-rate optimization.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure deflection and residual alignment after repeatable corner hits, and time a side-plate replacement without disturbing the roller assembly.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## 9470: floor redesign follows the scorer and service needs

Version: 9470 engineering reference and version history. [Technical source](https://9470techbinder.vercel.app/process/)

**Published construction:** Final floor has eight mixed-compliance rollers, one X60 and a two-screw pivot for access.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Simpler feeding and fast electronics service.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A floor that works for one shooter architecture may create unnecessary volume and transfer stages for another. Mixing hard tubes and compliant contacts can maintain support while encouraging fuel through a problematic region. The service pivot adds a deliberate state outside gameplay: technicians must be able to open the floor, reach electronics and restore alignment quickly. That can improve event reliability more than reducing a small amount of mass. Include cable routing, fastener retention and the post-service check in the architecture record.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Time an actual electrical repair through the pivot, then verify floor alignment and feeding after repeated open/close cycles.

## 9470: empirical calibration and practice deadline

Version: 9470 engineering reference and version history. [Technical source](https://9470techbinder.vercel.app/process/)

**Published construction:** Interpolated shot map, measured first-shot correction and time-of-flight lookahead; fixed pre-event ship deadline.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** An empirical map can be a technically rigorous choice when it captures the dominant real-world exit behavior within the available build window. It still needs enough sampling, a stable mechanical reference and a policy for replacing worn surfaces or changing fuel. The deadline is part of the architecture’s feasibility: every additional mechanism competes with the time needed to calibrate and drive it. A borrowed model should include its data-collection procedure and failure fallback rather than promising accuracy from a published algorithm name.

title: Reading technical evidence as an architecture agent
text:
# Reading technical evidence as an architecture agent

The mechanism notes separate five layers: published construction, the team's stated reason, original engineering interpretation, a proposed validation test, and remaining limits. The analysis is not an undisclosed quote from the team. A detailed explanation of why a contact or load path can work is not proof that the team measured that effect. When the source merely lists specifications, the stated-reason field explicitly says so. Do not convert a plausible mechanical explanation into a historical claim about the team's intent.

source_locator.section: Reading technical evidence as an architecture agent

title: A useful technical description follows the piece and the load
text:
## A useful technical description follows the piece and the load

For an intake, identify the first powered contact, the supporting surface, the point where ownership becomes secure and every transition before storage. State the acquisition envelope and the failure when the piece arrives diagonally, at a wall, in a pile or at maximum approach speed. A wide mouth can have a narrow effective capture area if its outer contacts eject rather than center. A motor count does not reveal whether a dead zone interrupts ownership. Record material, wheel geometry, compression, power transmission, deployment kinematics and the structure that reacts an impact as separate facts.

For a transfer, follow the piece through narrowing, turning, orientation and staging. Each imposed constraint should remove an unwanted degree of freedom without adding an over-constrained state. An unpowered surface can be useful guidance or the dominant drag source. An agitator can release a bridge or repeatedly throw the piece away from the receiving contact. A funnel and a singulator solve different problems. Their useful rate must be evaluated at full, partial and nearly empty inventory, including an interrupted feed and a reverse.

For a shooter, identify the entry state, compression history, contact duration, wheel surface velocities, release angle and resulting translation and spin. Free wheel speed is not ball speed. A soft piece deforms and can slip; a flexible ring can enter the same nominal gap in several shapes. An additional backing roller can control spin while changing friction and packaging. The architecture should include a measured calibration process and the mechanical references that make it repeatable after service.

For a positioning mechanism, follow the force path from the piece through the end effector, joint, bearings, structure and chassis. Motor encoder accuracy does not measure output deflection or backlash. A stiff-looking plate can be attached through a flexible joint; a highly reduced gearbox can still have a weak final tooth or inadequate shaft support. Reducing mass far from an axis reduces inertia more than an equal reduction near it. Counterbalances reduce one load component while creating another angle-dependent force. State the complete motion and load condition before borrowing a ratio.

For a climber, distinguish acquisition, retention, lift, settling and power-off support. The load path changes during those phases. A hook that catches a rung is not necessarily the part that safely supports the final suspension. A winch that can lift the robot can still rotate it into an illegal or damaging contact if the chain line is far from the center of mass. Shared-joint climbs couple primary scoring damage to endgame reliability. In 2026 the strategic default remains fuel-first and low-priority climb, even when the hardware itself is interesting.

source_locator.section: A useful technical description follows the piece and the load

title: First-order calculations are checks, not performance certifications
text:
## First-order calculations are checks, not performance certifications

Surface speed is approximately `v = pi * D * RPM / 60` when diameter and time units are consistent. At the same shaft speed, changing diameter changes both surface speed and the torque needed to produce a given contact force. A reduction improves output torque while lowering output speed; a tooth-count pair must be interpreted in the team's stated driver/driven order. This corpus preserves source notation where direction is ambiguous. Do not silently invert it or turn a free-speed calculation into loaded performance.

For a rotating joint, gravity torque is approximately the sum of each mass times gravitational acceleration times its perpendicular moment arm. Dynamic torque also includes inertia times angular acceleration and friction. A long telescoping arm changes both moment arm and inertia through its stroke. A final reduction, shaft and bearing must react the load even when several motors share the input. Mechanical advantage can vary sharply through a linkage, so checking only the endpoints can miss the highest force.

Flywheel stored energy is `E = 0.5 * I * omega^2`. That explains why inertia can buffer a short launch impulse, but does not prove a heavier flywheel improves recovery or total score. Motor power must replace the average energy, and extra inertia costs spin-up energy and mass. Recovery also depends on the controller, transmission, compression and timing of the next ball. A shooter can perform well with low added inertia if its motor authority and contact state are appropriate. Preserve counterexamples rather than turning one champion's design into a universal prescription.

For a complete fuel path, the minimum capacity of its serial services provides only an optimistic ceiling. Arrival gaps, bursty supply, jams and motion can reduce output well below that minimum. A nearly empty hopper can expose a different bottleneck from a full one. Track delivered scored fuel per usable interval, not just bench BPS. For coral, track a full acquisition-to-next-acquisition cycle and the probability of a retained legal score. The fastest isolated joint motion is not automatically the fastest useful task.

source_locator.section: First-order calculations are checks, not performance certifications

title: Tests should distinguish competing explanations
text:
## Tests should distinguish competing explanations

If an intake jams, record which contact first stops and whether a shaft, belt or guide moved. Change one compression or support dimension and reproduce the failed approach. If a shooter misses, separate localization error, hood-reference error, wheel recovery and ball-entry variation before changing the shot map. If a lift oscillates, measure both encoder tracking and physical tip motion. If an expanding hopper fails, test a loaded interrupted transition rather than only repeating empty endpoint moves.

Useful reported quantities include sample count, piece condition, battery voltage, configuration, setup and failure definition. Team-reported rates and movement times retain that label. A requirement table is not a results table; grey or unmet targets in a binder must not be imported as achievements. A CAD image is evidence of a design, not proof of a competed installation. A later rebuild must not overwrite the earlier robot. The all-125 binder audit distinguishes a located publication, accessible technical pages, a false association and an unresolved search; none establishes that every possible binder has been found.

title: Recommendation output
text:
## Recommendation output

Start with the game state and intended alliance role. State the measurable task goals, then name year/version-specific inspirations and the physical interfaces that must be redesigned. Include a positive reason and a failure mode for each major mechanism choice. Compare at least one coherent alternative under the same partner, supply, defense and development assumptions. Conclude with the smallest integrated experiment that could change the architecture decision. A recommendation that sounds fluent in team numbers but omits these conditions has not met the purpose of this database.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview describes a two-X44 intake at 2.5:1, passive carbon upper roller, roller-floor transmission described as 17:19, and a 3-inch steel drum driven by four X60s with powered hood rollers. A previously powered upper feed roller was made passive after jamming. Drum-region compression is reported as 3/8 inch and final roller compression as 1/2 inch.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly connects the stepped compression to fitting a replacement shooter in the existing robot, and the passive roller change to avoiding fuel being driven downward into jams. Collector repair access is deliberate because it receives impacts.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The important reference is the sequence of contacts, not simply four launcher motors. Upstream acceleration reduces the velocity increment demanded of the drum, while the passive restraint prevents one contact from injecting fuel into an already occupied region. More powered surfaces can therefore lower useful flow. A retrofit also fixes the available path length and elevation; its compression distribution cannot safely be transplanted without the same incoming velocity and support geometry. Separately, the agitation priority hierarchy means collector deployment and automatic shooting agitation are competing commands rather than independent subsystems.

title: Published / retained construction account

## Published / retained construction account

The interview distinguishes a former divided two-lane/double-spindexer arrangement from the drum rebuild with a roller floor. A powered lower intake roller was replaced by two 3/4-inch aluminum shafts with reduced compression. Compliant wheels near entry feed a J-shaped path; a guide was added after WPI wobble. title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team reports improved throughput after reducing collector compression, adds the guide to control observed motion, and describes reduced belt tension as a current-draw improvement. Driver controls were intentionally simplified around repeatable actions.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This is evidence against treating maximum grip as maximum throughput. Too many opposing powered contacts can trap deformable fuel or make its entry velocity inconsistent. Removing a roller changes the entire force chain, so the improvement should not be generalized to a collector with different ground geometry. Likewise, the software shoot command is a sequencer rather than a simultaneous motor-on command. Feeding early can pull down wheel speed or create an inaccurate initial volley, while waiting unnecessarily long reduces usable shift time.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The interview reports approximately 115-fuel capacity, a 33.5×21.375-inch robot envelope before the described extension, a wide 3-inch two-X60 intake, a load shield above the collector, and hopper structure changed from angle to tube. A two-position hood changed from pneumatic to linear actuation; wheel speed covers intermediate distances. Custom modules allow ratio changes and were geared down for the loaded robot.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The second collector motor and load shield respond to stalling and hopper pressure. Tube structure responds to racking and snagging. The lower drive ratio is explicitly tied to moving a heavily loaded robot across bumps with less stalling/current; the source attributes the actuator change to weight.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Capacity is useful only if it remains mobile and unloads reliably. A large stored column presses on its lowest contact surfaces, so a shield can be more valuable than another nominally faster roller. The hopper bar cutout and wheel sizing belong to the same route-clearance problem: a robot that can collect a full load but beaches on the bump loses the strategic value of that load. Two hood positions simplify mechanism travel, but the remaining range must be supplied by speed without creating unacceptable release-angle or recovery-time sensitivity.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test acceleration, bump traversal, braking, tip margin and current at empty/half/full inventory. Measure sustained unload rate rather than dividing nominal capacity by the fastest initial volley. Verify exact dimensions and the source gear notation in CAD.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The interview distinguishes the former turret from a four-X60 drum rebuild. A long kicker ramp maintains contact; a stub-roller floor pivots with the collector, with a jackshaft inside a roller. Passive hopper/net expansion is reported as roughly 50–55 fuel unexpanded and up to 78 expanded. A 1.5-lb steel flywheel with a stated 1:3 transmission supplements launcher inertia. The planned L1 mechanism was removed at inspection.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team attributes the ramp to sustained compression, the added flywheel to speed droop while feeding a large load, and climb removal to a discrepancy between shop and event weighing. A revised hood ratio sought a compromise between actuation speed and resistance to disturbance.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The supplementary flywheel stores energy in the motor-to-drum system; its contribution depends on the square of its speed ratio. That does not establish a sustained power budget, so a high first-volley rate may still decay. The pivoting floor improves access but introduces moving shaft/alignment interfaces. The source caption calls one small drum dimension ambiguously; do not infer diameter from that wording. Likewise, a removed climber is an unfielded feature for the filmed configuration, not an autonomous capability.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The collector deploy angle was flattened after first-event jams. The retained interview account describes surgical tubing replaced by grippier floor surfaces after fuel debris caused slip. The shooter uses a four-X60 aluminum drum, powered upper rollers and a compact geared steel flywheel; transfer is sequenced after launcher speed is reached. Current, voltage and temperature logging inform operating limits.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links the added flywheel to reduced speed decay and improved end-of-hopper accuracy. Floor/collector changes respond to observed jamming and contamination, while software limiting responds to the total electrical demand.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A material choice can work with clean practice fuel yet fail when loose surface debris changes friction. A flywheel can smooth a transient without fixing an inadequate recharge rate or a hot motor. The useful design reference is therefore a tested material/contact path plus an explicit electrical budget, not a motor count. Robot logging should distinguish commanded voltage, actual bus voltage, current limit, speed error and fuel flow; otherwise starvation and electrical saturation can look like the same shooting symptom.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Repeat full-hopper tests with used fuel and low batteries. Compare surface cleanliness, slip, speed recovery and motor temperature over multiple shifts rather than a single successful volley.

# 2026-7769: Passive feed solved one jam while rack durability remained unresolved

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2026-7769: Passive feed solved one jam while rack durability remained unresolved

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The rack collector and belt floor feed an originally divided shooter that became one continuous drum. In the team’s later technical discussion, powered upper/lower indexing rollers overpacked the ramp; immobilizing the lower rollers corrected that feed issue. The static hood avoids an exposed powered-roller belt. The team separately reports repeated polycarbonate rack-tooth failures and a 45-A deploying/5-A deployed current-limit strategy at Worlds.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The stated priorities are simple, durable mechanisms and resistance to trench contact. The lower surface was made static to meter entry rather than forcing fuel into a congested ramp. The current-limit change aimed to let the intake collapse under impact; failures became less frequent but did not disappear.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This example needs two distinct failure histories. A feed-path change can be successful while the deployment structure remains unreliable. Stronger propulsion is not automatically the fix for a packing jam, and a high-performing alliance run does not certify rack durability. Source-reported storage also has a useful distinction: almost 70 geometric capacity versus commonly 50–60 in play. Protected interior PETG vector wheels surviving a season is not evidence that the same prints would survive as exposed intake wheels.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test the passive lower feed with full hopper pressure and varied fuel. Instrument deployment impact/current and inspect tooth-root damage. A proposed decoupling of intake sides is a future idea, not a fielded fix.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A slotted three-roller transfer provides adjustable compression before a two-X60 high-inertia launcher. The flexible Hopper Flopper compresses under the trench and re-expands afterward. The shooter was reversed relative to the original robot, and the feeder speed varies with launcher speed error. The interview explicitly reports no climb.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links trench access to losing neutral-zone fuel races, preserving capacity to avoiding a smaller fixed hopper, and reversed orientation to reducing the need to turn after acquisition. Transfer modulation is intended to give fuel sufficient energy transfer while maintaining accuracy.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A compliant storage envelope changes which routes are available, so its value cannot be measured only in added fuel. It can change autonomous arrival order and the opponent’s available supply. Speed-error-dependent feed is a form of demand management: slow entry when the launcher is behind instead of allowing a nominally high feed command to create low-energy misses. The caption’s flywheel mass arithmetic is inconsistent, so preserve the qualitative high-inertia claim and seek a published mass breakdown rather than silently choosing one number.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare route arrival times, full-load trench passage, recovery after contact, and total scored fuel with fixed versus variable feeding. Measure sustained and initial BPS separately.

text:
## Limits

Interview plus team replies in topic 515730. The first release reports about 15–16 BPS over a full roughly 80-fuel hopper versus around 20–25 initially; these are team reports for that configuration, not measurements of every later revision.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The interview describes a passively deploying intake/hopper, roller floor explicitly inspired by 2017 team 254, a separate feed stage, a four-X60 launcher and added brass flywheel inertia. The hood is fixed; distance changes use speed and chassis aim. Intake motion agitates the stored fuel, and the aiming system has a manual fallback.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly credits the historical floor reference and identifies the fallback as a way to keep playing when automatic aim fails. No team-stated numerical optimum for fixed hood angle is established in this passage.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Removing hood actuation reduces moving hardware, but does not remove aiming requirements. The usable trajectory envelope is now constrained by wheel speed, launch angle, release height, accuracy and the routes from which the chassis can point at the target. The passive deployment also makes initial orientation and autonomous motion part of the mechanism’s operation. A simple subsystem can therefore demand careful whole-match planning without being a poor design.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

Roman I uses a rotating floor/center drum and turret; first-party replies describe a roughly 20.75-inch outer drum and 6-inch center, with no fuel compression. Roman II replaces that path with a full-width roller floor and drum shooter. Its floor pivots about an intake dead shaft for electronics access; long four-bar arms fold under impact. The interview contrasts roughly 8 BPS before the rebuild with a reported 23 afterward.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The strategic change is not simply a faster wheel. Storage, feed width, shooting heading, electrical packaging and intake structure changed together. A comparison should include time spent aiming and avoiding defense, not only an unloaded discharge rate. The original no-compression spindexer and later low-compression drum entry must not be merged into an imaginary hybrid. Service access is especially useful after a rebuild because new routing and wiring require frequent inspection.

## Proposed validation — not performed

# 2026-5687: Capstan deployment and belt-floor lanes are dated fixes, not universal upgrades

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2026-5687: Capstan deployment and belt-floor lanes are dated fixes, not universal upgrades

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

First-party replies describe 2-inch upper rollers, a 1.25-inch lower roller and about half an inch of compression. The robot changed from roller floor to belt floor between URI and UVM, and from rack deployment to a rope capstan after tooth damage. A 6-inch, 1/8-inch-wall aluminum drum was urethane-coated, machined and balanced; its reported inertia is a little over 80 lb·in².

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team says lower collector compression reduced motor bogging. It reports lower current and faster feeding after the belt-floor change; belt spacing created lanes and reduced fuel spinning in place. Rope deployment addressed rack tooth failures, with rope tension becoming the continuing adjustment.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This is a useful counterexample to choosing a floor from appearance alone. Belt spacing can organize deformable fuel and remove an unproductive rotating contact state, but that result depends on piece size, belt spacing, load and friction. A capstan cannot skip discrete gear teeth, yet it can slip, stretch, lose tension or suffer anchor damage. The team’s prior capstan experience also changes development risk: the decision was supported by an existing implementation history rather than an untested mechanism adopted casually midseason.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test lane stability, residual fuel, electrical demand and rope tension after repeated impacts. Preserve the report that auto shot timers shortened by over half a second without inventing exact before/after BPS.

title: Limits
text:
## Limits

Selected first-party replies 14, 16, 21, 23, 38, 40 and 42 in topic 515683, plus code-release topic 524737. This is a discussion/code-release review, not a reviewed technical binder.

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

First-party replies describe separate X44s for indexer and spindexer, a spinning floor/cone with no deliberate wall compression, and multiple feeder-wheel and ratio trials. The third intake version adds a kicker and movable secondary kicker. The shooter lacks an upper roller; its moving-shot solution combines tuned lookup data and a physics calculation that compensates for spin.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team says the movable kicker resolves earlier collector difficulty and clarifies that the feeder delivers fuel without spin. It does not provide a definitive causal explanation for all of the achieved spindexer throughput. The added flood light helps close-range tag reliability rather than substantially increasing long-range detection.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The absence of a counter-roller makes spin an explicit aiming input rather than something to assume away. A compact turret may leave more free hopper area, but the detailed explanation of dead zones and geometry offered by another commenter is expressly an outsider’s hypothesis. Keep that hypothesis separate from the team’s replies. Successful self-unjamming also does not mean jams never occur; the source explicitly acknowledges occasional jams.

text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure entrance spin and moving-shot error across turret angles, record jam/recovery frequency and time, and inspect exact CAD before copying clearances or interpreting an image-based diameter estimate.

A floor hard stop can define a repeatable pickup plane, but should not be confused with clearance throughout the rest of the motion. Thin coral tolerates less forced compression than foam fuel, so roller selection must be paired with a controlled guide gap.

# 2025-604: Precision depends on stiffness, backlash and feeding order

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-604: Precision depends on stiffness, backlash and feeding order

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A single-stage elevator is driven by chains on both sides to reduce twist; the arm/wrist and shimmed transmissions aim to minimize backlash. The large corrugated-plastic station funnel damps entry. Independently stopped feed rollers can hold coral while the gripper handles algae, and a compact climber fits beneath the funnel.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly treats accuracy as a mechanical and software requirement, identifies dual-sided elevator drive with resisting twist, and explains pausing coral feed during algae possession.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A vision system can command the correct pose yet miss a branch if the scoring frame deflects or the transmission reverses through backlash. Hybrid cycles add a scheduling constraint: the incoming coral must not collide with a manipulator that is still gripping algae. The funnel and climber also compete for the same physical space, so a copied climber cannot be assumed to fit behind another team’s station system.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure effector displacement under lateral load and direction reversal; test queued coral while holding algae. Compare repeatability after repeated elevator cycles and drivetrain impacts.

# 2025-694: A dedicated low-task arm adds work without monopolizing the elevator

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-694: A dedicated low-task arm adds work without monopolizing the elevator

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The station funnel uses powered surfaces and an IR entry sensor. The separate Froggy mechanism acquires coral/algae from the floor and scores L1/processor; its source gives a 48:1 X60 pivot and 2:1 X60 roller drive. A linked shaft/chain keeps the side plates synchronized, while added angle reinforcement stiffens their weak direction.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes reinforcement after structural analysis and a software interlock that delays retracting Froggy until the chassis backs away from the reef. The main arm’s motor placement is also used for counterbalance.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Low-level work can justify a dedicated mechanism when it shortens cycles and releases the primary scorer for another role. That benefit is conditional on interference: two mechanisms must be able to store, acquire and move without colliding. A geometric safety interlock should therefore be part of the architecture reference. “Button released” is not sufficient evidence that an external mechanism can retract safely.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test concurrent main-arm/Froggy poses, compare complete L1/algae cycles, and verify retreat detection before retraction under localization error.

# 2025-1678: Wide pickup, light elevator and faster cage capture solve different delays

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-1678: Wide pickup, light elevator and faster cage capture solve different delays

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A wide four-bar collector feeds the lightweight coral/algae effector on a string-driven continuous elevator. The interview describes thicker carbon after a week-five collector member bent and cracked; the caption does not safely establish the thickness. Later cage guides and capture wheels replace a slower alignment approach.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links width to driver tolerance, elevator construction to speed/weight/CG, and the revised cage capture to reducing an approximately twenty-second climb process toward roughly ten seconds.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The motorized scoring cycle is only one part of match throughput. Wide acquisition can reduce driver correction, while a faster endgame can recover entire scoring cycles. Those gains can justify mass in guides or reinforcement even when they increase subsystem weight. The original and revised climb should not be averaged into one time, and the gain should not be applied to a team whose approach geometry differs.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure failed-pickup rate, full extension deflection and complete cage-approach-to-secured time. Repeat impact tests on the reinforced collector instead of assuming more carbon fixes every load direction.

# 2025-1690: Differential arm/elevator motion keeps motors low but couples control

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-1690: Differential arm/elevator motion keeps motors low but couples control

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The source describes an efficient floor collector, V-shaped powered centering path and a differential elevator/arm transmission. Equal coordinated belt motion translates the carriage; differential motion changes arm angle while the motors stay low. The retained technical record also describes a custom-sealed suction effector and piston/scotch-yoke vacuum source.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team’s explicit objective is short, fast coral cycles and resistance to defense without excessive sacrifice of algae capability. Keeping arm/elevator drive motors at the base serves low moving mass.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A differential does not eliminate shoulder or elevator effort; it redistributes that demand across shared actuators. Motion limits, current and saturation must be considered in joint space and motor space. The vacuum end effector can reduce exposed gripping hardware, but seal geometry and surface condition become critical. A short-cycle strategy also needs coordinated human-player supply and a path that avoids interference with partners.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test simultaneous lift/rotation near motor limits, vacuum retention on damaged or wet pieces, and recovery after a partially seated coral. Preserve emergency climb acceleration as a high-load exception, not the normal durability baseline.

# 2025-1706: Cable control and a later algae arm are essential version details

source_locator.section: 2025-1706: Cable control and a later algae arm are essential version details

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The robot retains an elevator-based station-fed scorer and later adds a compact curved-rack algae intake. A constant-force spring pulls the elevator cable carrier inward after it repeatedly broke, flopped outward or entered the funnel. The climber uses the funnel’s rear region and was revised to grab one cage bar.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes the algae arm as lightweight and quick to deploy, and identifies the spring as the response to cable-carrier failures. The updated climb seeks easier capture rather than a larger nominal grasp.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A cable carrier is a moving structural interface, not an afterthought in the electrical system. Its force, bend radius and free envelope affect elevator current and what can enter the station funnel. An added algae collector also changes the safe pose space of an already working scorer. The architecture should retain the dated add-on history rather than imply the final robot existed at the first event.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Run full-stroke cable fatigue tests and check the spring at maximum extension. Test coral loading with the algae mechanism deployed and verify cage capture under angular misalignment.

# 2025-1771: Wrist freedom creates L1 value and a collision-planning obligation

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-1771: Wrist freedom creates L1 value and a collision-planning obligation

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The team explicitly credits 4414’s 2023 continuous elevator. Its carriage combines a pivot, wrist and compliant coral/algae end effector; range sensors and a transverse wheel actively center coral. The software models tested safe poses and allows only transitions connected in a graph.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The interview ties the wrist to effective L1 cycles and the pivot to serving both ground and station acquisition. The restricted transition graph is intended to prevent destructive arm/elevator interactions and overshoot.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The wrist should not be justified only by branch reach. It also changes how coral can be presented to the trough, so its value can rise in a low-task alliance role. The price is a larger configuration space: correct endpoint poses do not prove that the path between them is safe. A tested edge graph is a concrete way to carry mechanical clearance assumptions into software.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Test every allowed transition under lag, sensor error and simultaneous chassis motion. Measure L1 throughput as well as L4 reach, and verify active centering before the final placement motion.

# 2025-1778: Game simulation preceded the ground-intake commitment

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-1778: Game simulation preceded the ground-intake commitment

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A narrow initial ground concept became a wide collector, feeding an internally belted elevator and arm that can score toward either side. The team reports offseason experience with similar mechanisms. Each software state specifies the collector, elevator, arm and roller setpoints together, with explicit transition conditions.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes running match simulations on day two after kickoff to test the significance of unprotected station defense. It connects the floor collector to that strategic result and the monolithic state structure to predictable safe motion.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This is a process reference as much as a hardware reference. The team tested a game constraint before committing to a cycle architecture, then used known mechanism families to reduce development risk. Wide acquisition helps only when the handoff can keep up and the arm can safely retract past both field and robot structure. A multi-subsystem state should retain possession information so a timing variation does not silently drop coral.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Repeat the strategic simulation with plausible opposing and partner robots. Test interrupted transfers and safe recovery from each intermediate state, rather than validating only the nominal score sequence.

# 2025-2481: Floor orientation and a moving scorer share the alignment workload

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-2481: Floor orientation and a moving scorer share the alignment workload

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The collector uses one motor, a passive guide wall and wheel/roller contact to orient floor coral without a separate vertical-roller stage. A chain-driven lateral slide on Igus guides corrects scorer position. A cascade elevator and custom drivetrain complete the retained architecture.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly connects floor pickup to human players rolling coral near the reef. Its custom-module discussion emphasizes traction and useful gearing rather than adopting an unmodified commercial package.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A passive orienter exchanges actuator count for sensitivity to incoming pose, wall friction and driving direction. A lateral scorer can remove some last-meter chassis correction, but it must be stiff enough that the camera’s intended offset corresponds to the actual end-effector position. Ground-source supply and local correction should therefore be assessed as one cycle, including the human player’s delivery error.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Sample many coral approach orientations and supply distances. Measure lateral-slide backlash/deflection under acceleration, and compare whole-cycle time against a fixed scorer with chassis-only alignment.

# 2025-3005: A serializer rebuild must eliminate stable wrong orientations

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-3005: A serializer rebuild must eliminate stable wrong orientations

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

Before Worlds, passive polycarbonate funneling and one lower belt were replaced by molded powered flaps that contact awkward coral orientations. The retained ladder-style placement mechanism also received a cam after early L4 tipping/alignment difficulties. The interview separately describes a ratcheting climb that can retain partial progress after disable.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The serializer change is explicitly tied to coral settling into specific trapped orientations. Retaining a climb after power-off is described as an important requirement, not an incidental effect of gearing.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A funnel that succeeds in the common orientation can still create a stable mechanical equilibrium in an uncommon one. Powered flaps need to disturb that equilibrium without ejecting or crushing the piece. Likewise, an L4 scorer should be judged by placement stability and alignment delay, not only reaching the nominal height. These are distinct revisions and should not be attributed to one unchanging opening-week robot.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Deliberately place coral in every previously trapped pose, measure recovery time, and test L4 placement after abrupt chassis stops. Verify retention with the actual disabled climb configuration.

# 2025-3663: A sideways elevator makes pass-through feasible with different interference

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-3663: A sideways elevator makes pass-through feasible with different interference

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The fourth arm/grabber iteration works beside a sideways-oriented elevator. The robot handles coral levels and algae with the same arm assembly. The interview also describes placing the battery to counter the elevator’s mass and moving the scoring arm clear during climbing.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says it wanted pass-through behavior but did not consider passing through the elevator suitable for its resources. It identifies low center of gravity as a reason for the alternate arrangement.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Pass-through is a functional requirement, not a mandate to send the piece through an elevator opening. An offset mechanism can provide the desired acquisition/scoring directions while changing lateral load, frame torsion and the safe sweep envelope. Counterweight placement may improve static balance but should be checked throughout arm travel and with each game piece.

text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure lateral deflection and tip margin in the highest off-center pose; test all arm-to-climber transitions. Do not infer an undisclosed collector construction from the functional pass-through description.

# 2025-3683: Station retention, orientation recovery and fast lift must work together

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2025-3683: Station retention, orientation recovery and fast lift must work together

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A post-Niagara ramp/retention change reduces coral bounce-out and permits longer-distance station delivery. Two sensors support orientation detection and unjamming, while the ramp can queue coral during algae possession. The internally belted three-stage elevator has two low motors and tie-rod stiffening; the team reports slightly over half a second to full extension.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source ties the ramp revision directly to entry bounce and the tie rods to rigidity. The retained record describes using an upper roller to redirect coral for L1 as well as higher-level scoring.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A fast unloaded lift is valuable only if the queued piece remains controlled and the effector settles accurately. Keeping the next coral on the ramp while holding algae can remove travel from the next cycle, but requires distinct possession states and a deliberate handoff. The reported lift time should remain a mechanism claim rather than a full-cycle time.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure loaded settle time, queued-piece retention during lift motion, and unjamming success for sideways coral. Check cable retention over repeated rapid extensions.

title: Published / retained construction account

A shared pinch claw can reduce moving mechanisms but its force and retained orientation must remain acceptable for two very different pieces.

# 2025-5990: Protected power and adjustable rigging support a ground-source cycle

source_locator.section: 2025-5990: Protected power and adjustable rigging support a ground-source cycle

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

The two-stage floor intake keeps its motor inside the chassis, then uses a belt and centering wheel to orient coral. A fixture/beam-break locates the handoff. The continuous elevator has two motors and wrench-adjustable ratchet tensioners for its ropes; a rack positions the shared gripper.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly connects internal motor placement to preventing collision damage and the ratchet arrangement to maintaining rope tension. The interview also demonstrates vision-based coral acquisition.

title: Engineering interpretation — analyst inference
text:
## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A protected motor still transmits impact through shafts and belts, so the whole load path needs inspection. Adjustable rigging is useful when it makes a repeatable service procedure possible; excessive or unequal tension can add friction and rack a carriage. Vision-directed pickup should be evaluated with the mechanical centering tolerance rather than as an independent AI success.

title: Proposed validation — not performed
text:
## Proposed validation — not performed

Document a reproducible rope-tension procedure, check left/right travel under load, and test handoff after impacts. Measure acquisition success with occlusion and adjacent pieces.

title: Published / retained construction account

The arm retains an A-frame/shoulder architecture and reduces the telescope to one moving stage. A guided arm-end collector sends notes directly into the top/bottom-wheel launcher; extension is used for amp and trap. Multiple pose cameras and a note-detection camera support acquisition and scoring.

Reducing extension stages can remove mass, cable length, backlash and maintenance points while retaining the needed task envelope. The comparison must use actual amp/trap geometry and the stage clearance rules, not maximum theoretical arm reach. Direct note handling avoids transfer errors but carries the launcher’s mass and flexible note through the arm’s motion.

# 2024-604: Controlled centering preserves deliberately asymmetric shooting contact

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

source_locator.section: 2024-604: Controlled centering preserves deliberately asymmetric shooting contact

title: Published / retained construction account
text:
## Published / retained construction account

A wide compliant/dead-axis intake and guides center the note before an asymmetric launcher contact sequence. The same scoring assembly handles amp delivery and rises for trap work. Beam-break acquisition feedback retracts the collector and rumbles the driver controller.

title: Team-stated reasoning or boundary
text:
## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

This history explains why commanded angle, measured motor angle and true launcher angle are different quantities. Increasing control gains cannot reliably fix a slipping transmission. The early proposal to climb using the shooter must remain a proposal unless later installation evidence supports it.

title: 1. Kickoff: rank incentives differ from point value
text:
## 1. Kickoff: rank incentives differ from point value

[Navigation 150–395 s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1UsbJD-zRjU&t=150)

**Source account / attributed commentary:** The commentator compares match points with the ease of earning different ranking points. In his retrospective, leave-plus-one-coral and a deep climb plus park appear relatively accessible, making coral-level completion an important qualifier differentiator.

**Conditional interpretation — analyst reasoning:** This is a prediction framework tied to a field of teams, not an immutable task ranking. If a bonus becomes routine, its marginal ranking value falls even though its point value is unchanged. Evaluate the expected event population and rule revision before allocating mechanism effort.

title: 2. Why algae looked unattractive early

title: Retained full-caption account
text:
## Retained full-caption account

The synthesis revisits alternating algae/coral, defensive leverage and a defender’s escape path. It forecasts alliance construction and discusses New England district-point routes: strong results, a valuable second-pick role or accumulating enough points across events. Historical New England examples are not numerical Peachtree thresholds.

title: 1. Dual-resource offense makes defensive target selection harder

## 1. Dual-resource offense makes defensive target selection harder

[Navigation 293–358 s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ciCaO4_So9o&t=293)

**Source account / attributed commentary:** The synthesis returns to partners alternating coral and algae so that a defender moving across the field can arrive at an obsolete target.

**Conditional interpretation — analyst reasoning:** The tactic works through useful alternate work and travel cost. If the defender can cover both paths or the alternate task is exhausted, the advantage may disappear. Track resource availability and partner congestion.

title: 2. The defender also needs an exit and a useful central posture

## 2. The defender also needs an exit and a useful central posture

**Conditional interpretation — analyst reasoning:** A defensive position has to support the next interaction, not merely win the current push. Avoid advice that depends on a pin or foul interpretation without checking the rule and the observed contact.

title: How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis
text:
# How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU

Published: 2026-05-04. Review: 2026-10-25. Automatic English captions; 1388 timestamped segments. Every exported caption was read. The final caption begins at 46:19; this is not a video-duration measurement. No raw transcript is redistributed. No visual audit was possible.

A complete available-caption study of the upper-bracket final and all three 2026 Einstein finals. The central account is the coupling of autonomous contact, transition position, neutral-zone supply, steal timing, shoot-on-the-move passing and 4065’s defensive geometry. Breakdowns and uncertain intent remain explicit confounders.

Compare whole alliance control loops, not drum rate against turret rate in isolation. A robot can make a smaller immediate score while changing who owns the next supply of fuel, who can arrive before a shift starts and which opponent must cross a defended bottleneck. The source’s counterfactual wins and point-denial estimates are hypotheses, not measured individual contributions.

source_locator.section: How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis

title: 0:07–0:35 · Scope, alliance identities and the danger of rewriting the series as a clean architecture contest

## 0:07–0:35 · Scope, alliance identities and the danger of rewriting the series as a clean architecture contest

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=7s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 0:07–0:35 · Scope, alliance identities and the danger of rewriting the series as a clean architecture contest

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The introduction treats the upper-bracket meeting plus three finals as one strategic series. Daly fields 4065, 4414 and 1323; Newton fields 868, 2046 and 2910. The creator credits both Daly’s scoring pair and 4065’s defense. Later passages explicitly describe interruptions to 1323, 868 and 2046. The account therefore contains several changing robot-availability states rather than four repetitions of the same six healthy machines.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

An architecture comparison should condition on operational state. A two-turret alliance beating two dumpers in the final result does not establish an unconditional turret advantage: starting positions, autonomous contact, defensive assignments, fuel distribution and failures all change between matches. Conversely, describing the series only as breakdowns discards the account of deliberate supply control. Preserve both explanations until footage and team logs can separate them. The six active robots are the match-specific roster; a reserve on the championship alliance must not be silently treated as an active participant in these four recordings.

title: 0:35–3:28 · Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route
text:
## 0:35–3:28 · Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=35s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 0:35–3:28 · Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The creator describes 1323 beginning at an angle and cutting ahead of 2910 rather than first translating sideways. He says this leaves one corner of fuel but permits a larger sweep around the pile. He attributes 2910’s later misalignment and intake corner catching to the rotation caused by that encounter. On the other side, 4414 makes a central pass with a following 4065 route, collects near the hub wall and returns to score from the outpost side. He connects 4414’s net and hopper to retaining a large collection across the bump and clearing it before autonomous ends. His belief that the teams timed the opposing routes is explicitly an assumption.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

The useful design requirement is an autonomous system whose acquisition envelope, collision recovery and route compatibility are evaluated together. A route can abandon a small pocket yet improve total possession by reaching a more valuable arc first. A high collection rate can create an exit-path problem if the loaded robot cannot traverse the selected obstacle without shedding fuel. A net is therefore part of the mobility–storage interface, not an isolated capacity feature. None of this gives a dimension, actual retained count or certified causal diagnosis of 2910’s auto error. Reproduce the route interaction with synchronized overhead video and logs before concluding that the same cut always defeats the same opponent.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The account praises 4065 for ending near midfield and immediately reaching across to contest Newton’s transition fuel. It contrasts 868 ending deeper on its own side and arriving after 1323 and 4414 have already collected and moved ahead of it. The commentator argues that a defender arriving late misses a short opportunity to reduce the autonomous winner’s transition scoring. He describes Daly converting its uncontested collection into sustained transition output.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Treat autonomous terminal pose as the initial condition of teleop, including the defender. Maximizing a small autonomous contribution may be a poor trade if it places that robot too far from the next high-value interception. The source describes a timing window, not a universal instruction to send a defender immediately across the field. The outcome depends on the actual active-hub schedule, legal routes, expected collector arrival and whether intercepting one scorer leaves a partner free. Official fuel confirms a 65–30 transition advantage for Daly in this match, but that alliance total cannot measure the individual value of 4065’s terminal pose or prove the stated cause.

title: 5:14–9:00 · Upper bracket first active shifts: dual moving passers clean supply while imposing incidental delay

## 5:14–9:00 · Upper bracket first active shifts: dual moving passers clean supply while imposing incidental delay

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=314s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 5:14–9:00 · Upper bracket first active shifts: dual moving passers clean supply while imposing incidental delay

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The creator describes 1323 and 4414 splitting the neutral zone, circling through fuel and passing it back while their hub is inactive. They also occupy enough of 2046’s path to make acquisition awkward. He contrasts this with a dumper stopping to pass a batch. In his account, 2046 finds little fuel in the neutral zone, returns toward its own corner reserves and later has difficulty obtaining another hopper. He mentions 868 holding fuel and a 4065 blocker delaying part of 2910’s final discharge.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

This is a coupled acquisition, passing and interference role. Passing while moving can let an off-shift robot keep collecting instead of serializing collect, stop, orient and release; the same motion can close an opponent’s useful approach. That does not make every turret a good moving passer. Intake throughput, feed continuity, aiming under motion, range, loaded acceleration and the ability to keep fuel on the intended side all matter. Fuel temporarily held in a third robot is another supply state, even if that robot scores little. The source supplies neither a complete fuel ledger nor timing measurements, so avoid turning this account into a quantified claim that turrets always clean the field faster than drums.

title: 9:00–13:47 · Upper bracket: starvation changes departure location, which changes the next steal and partner release
text:
## 9:00–13:47 · Upper bracket: starvation changes departure location, which changes the next steal and partner release

[Source navigation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Cm-RuiSNlU&t=540s). These are commentary-video times, not match-clock times.

source_locator.section: 9:00–13:47 · Upper bracket: starvation changes departure location, which changes the next steal and partner release

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The analysis follows 2046 from an unproductive neutral-zone visit into a corner collection, then into a later cross-field steal. It says the later departure gives 1323 roughly three additional seconds before the steal arrives. In the other direction, 4414 can leave earlier to remove Newton’s stashed fuel. Later, 1323 screens 868 so 4414 can cross back, while 2046 again arrives late. The creator frames these actions as compounding consequences of the earlier neutral-zone cleanup, not independent isolated tricks.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Track location and inventory at every shift boundary. A robot with the same amount of fuel but a different terminal position can have a very different next assignment. Supply denial may first force a detour, then postpone a steal, then expose a partner’s prepared pile; simply counting immediate defended scoring seconds misses those downstream opportunities. The reported three-second gain remains an estimate from edited commentary. Alternative explanations include traffic, operator choice and recovery from previous contact. An auditable event log should separate observed departure, observed arrival, unknown fuel count and inferred causal link, rather than give one long causal sentence the status of a directly observed fact.

text:
### Attributed source account

This is an interesting mechanical hypothesis because the perimeter changes contact geometry and the moment generated by a push. It is not a proof that a rounded robot always has leverage or that polygons are always trapped. Real contact includes compliant bumpers, friction, traction limits, module directions, loaded inertia and nearby walls. A curved perimeter can also change packaging, bumper construction and available acquisition width. The transfer test should compare the complete loaded drivetrains and controlled contact angles. The pick reversal is a driver-training insight: a good defender needs escape practice as well as pursuit practice. Team intent and the exact curvature remain unverified without primary geometry and footage.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The commentary describes 1678 attempting a steal while its hopper is extended, making it bump-only at that instant. 6324 notices and interrupts the return rather than continuing to fill itself. The creator estimates 6324 has a much smaller load and 1678 a larger one; he says the delay consumes roughly the remaining useful scoring interval. He also acknowledges that 1678 still removes fuel from Johnson and could pass or score it later, so the steal is not automatically valueless.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Value the inventories on a schedule. Removing fifty hypothetical fuel from an opponent is not the same as adding fifty score now, and a delayed load can become exposed to a reciprocal steal. Likewise, a small hopper on a support robot is not automatically a reason to defend: the partner needs a current scoring window worth protecting, and the delay must survive the opponent’s available escape. The exact hopper counts and twelve-second estimate are not independently measured. A visual event log should mark the route block, changed configuration, attempted escapes, release and actual first scoring time, with unknown counts left null.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The creator describes 6324 screening to let 4946 leave while 1678 and 2481 collide or congest the middle. He then notes 6324 taking back fuel from Milstein’s side during part of its own scoring time. His explanation is that the neutral zone has become sparse partly because so much fuel is already held in 1678 and 2481. The initial Milstein steal has value, but the delayed use of that inventory allows Johnson to recover some of the supposed advantage.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

An alliance can be rich in fuel but poor in immediately accessible scoring opportunities. Large loaded hoppers reduce shared field supply for everybody, including the owner’s partners; an opponent with another reachable reserve may temporarily have the better play. This is a dynamic inventory and timing problem, not simply hopper capacity times shooter rate. The collision and screening intent still require footage. A useful agent should be able to explain why the same 6324 can screen, steal and score at different moments without collapsing those actions into a generic “support” paragraph or assuming every action was a preplanned call.

title: Attributed source account
text:
### Attributed source account

The source closes by following Johnson’s prepared corner fuel and loaded robots, Milstein’s late effort to find reserves and both Milstein scorers returning for final cycles. He interprets the remaining supply and shift order as the reason Johnson can win despite losing auto narrowly. He also gives a no-penalty comparison of 678–691. The final recorded match is 688–691 because Milstein receives ten penalty points. The commentary’s claim that the auto loser has the better teleop conditions is an interpretation of this match state.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Preserve both margins: three in the official final, thirteen in fuel or clean output, with the penalty difference identified. This close result is sensitive to many events besides active-shift order. Compare it to the upper-bracket Daly example: there, winning auto accompanies strong transition position and cleanup that deny the opponent an easy supply setup. Here, the source argues the auto winner does not maintain that control and also faces crossing and screening problems. The transferable principle is to model the next supply state and routes under either autonomous outcome. It is not that auto has negative value, and the source does not establish a universal optimal margin.

title: Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation
text:
### Conditional engineering or strategy interpretation

Do not use an outro claim to certify channel completeness. The database’s discovered-video list and canonical-match list need their own inventories, including alternate recordings and any replayed attempts. This study covers the two described canonical matches and the author’s defense theory, through the last available caption. It contains no new direct visual observations and cannot be used to clear a pending visual-audit flag.

title: Questions for verification
text:
## Questions for verification

- Why is an expanded 1678 hopper also a route constraint, and how does that change who should attempt a steal?
- How can 254 deliberately stop scoring briefly yet improve its alliance’s output later? What makes the claimed causal effect unverified?
- Why does 6324’s choice to delay a loaded 1678 differ from a generic instruction that every scorer should always defend?
- Explain the creator’s rounded-bumper hypothesis for 4946 and identify at least three reasons that a circle alone cannot guarantee escape.
- What is meant by a defender having to play offense against a partner’s pick, and what would you observe to distinguish an intentional pick from ordinary congestion?
- Compare this video’s “lose auto narrowly” thesis with the earlier Daly account of compounding an auto win. Under what different supply and route assumptions can both be reasonable?
- What are the official final and clean scores of match 6? Why must the three-point final margin not be substituted for the thirteen-point clean margin?

title: Remaining uncertainties
text:
## Remaining uncertainties

- This is an August retrospective of May matches, with knowledge of outcomes. It is not evidence that these lessons were already consensus during kickoff or early season.
- The complete available captions were read; the underlying footage did not render. No described collision, perimeter, shot, pin or route is independently visually verified in this pass.
- The captions corrupt Curie, team names and several numbers. 6800 is Valor, 8613 is Barker, 2481 is Roboteers, 4946 is Alpha Dogs; exact identifiers are normalized only where rosters and context establish them.
- The creator estimates hoppers, potential points and delay durations, and openly guesses autonomous prescouting intent. None is an independently counted robot contribution.
- The commentary’s effective 55-second endgame groups a preceding active shift with the shared final period for one alliance. It must not replace the official final-30-second score component or the rule definition.
- The author is unsure whether an apparent hold on 2481 is a pin and cannot see the hub-side contact. Do not turn this into a legal ruling.
- Rounded-perimeter escape is a hypothesis from this interaction, not proof of immunity to defense. Traction, friction, contact normal, module torque, field obstacles and loaded mass still require examination.
- A close match after an autonomous loss cannot demonstrate that intentionally losing auto is globally optimal. The hypothesis requires comparable alliances, margin, supply-control ability and opponent response.

text: # Einstein visual-audit protocol and current checkpoint
