title: What this edition actually establishes
text:
## What this edition actually establishes

The corpus contains 80 canonical Einstein match records across 2022–2026: 18, 15, 15, 16 and 16 respectively. All 80 have a candidate recording link after recovery of the official 2022 match-2 page. A canonical TBA match row is not a verified inventory of every played/replayed attempt or every camera angle. That additional completeness check remains open.

Zero visual match audits are complete. Six recording pages were opened for access/identity checks; the rest were not individually tested in this pass. Representative recordings from all five seasons supplied metadata but no decoded match frame, remaining black and buffering. Normal reload, playback controls, a lower quality on the 2022 player, seeking on the 2026 player and documented media export did not produce footage. The failure is specific to these tested sessions; it does not prove all videos are unavailable or identify a network cause. It was not a visible bot challenge in this session.

The user authorized solving the prior CAPTCHA. On opening the normal watch page there was no CAPTCHA to solve. The transcript interface worked. All eleven previously pending exports were recovered. Two new available-caption reads cover six canonical 2026 matches, with detailed attributed accounts and conditional analysis. Nine recovered exports still await full content review. The prior 33 caption studies retain their inherited review scope. Nothing in this checkpoint is represented as permanent internal model memory or as visual watching.

title: Identity before tactics
text:
## Identity before tactics

Compare the title, year, teams, alliance colors, bracket position and final score. A similar title or a mirror association is insufficient. The rejected 2022 match-2 link previously pointed to match 15. The replacement is the official FIRST recording titled “Einstein 2 - 2022 FIRST Championship”; its visible description exactly matches red 1619/6672/254 scoring 164 and blue 3534/5940/6328 scoring 122. This establishes page identity, not independent visual identity. Keep that distinction if the video is mislabeled or contains a replay later in the file.

For each recording, preserve its exact URL, creator, available duration and any alternate-angle relation. Record whether a replay is the final scored attempt or an abandoned/no-score attempt. Do not silently overwrite the original evidence when substituting a better angle. In 2022 the semifinal stage is round-robin-style Einstein play; later double-elimination set/match keys use different conventions. Do not infer bracket order by sorting all seasons with the same filename heuristic.

title: A continuous first pass plus six robot-follow passes
text:
## A continuous first pass plus six robot-follow passes

View the full match from prestart through the final action at a speed that preserves the interactions being asserted. Establish where autonomous starts, teleop starts and the match ends in the source video. Link every event to both source time and the visible match clock when available. For edited analysis with pauses, rewinds or slow motion, use a piecewise mapping rather than assuming source seconds equal elapsed match seconds. A caption timestamp is a navigation pointer until aligned visually.

Then follow each of the six robots through the full sequence. Record acquisition source, held inventory only when countable, scoring location and configuration, crossing choice, passing destination, screen/defense target and changes of job. For 2026, identify the actual hub state and the robot’s preparation for its next active window. For 2025, record concurrent L1, algae and branch work rather than imposing a serial “finish high branches, then do L1” story. For earlier seasons, preserve their own field geometry, scoring constraints and endgame incentives; do not import the 2026 supply model automatically.

A role is an interval, not a permanent label for a team or a robot. The same robot can score, pass, screen, steal, defend and recover in one match. A stopped robot can affect a route while providing no intended defensive action. A robot with a loaded hopper can influence supply without scoring. A defender may change targets to protect a crossing instead of following its original mark. Keep those possibilities distinguishable in the log.

source_locator.section: A continuous first pass plus six robot-follow passes

title: What an individual event needs
text:
## What an individual event needs

Store event ID, match key, recording ID, source start/end, match-clock start/end, actors, current configuration, field location, directly visible action, visible outcome, uncertainty and evidence links. Distinguish “robot contacts opponent,” “opponent changes route,” “shots fall short” and “robot stops moving.” Those observations do not by themselves mean “intentional pick,” “successful defense worth one hopper,” “battery sag” or “radio failure.” Put those interpretations in separate fields with their supporting or missing evidence.

For a screen or defensive handoff, observe all participants before and after the interaction. A five-second delay may save another defender’s travel, but it may also cost the screening scorer an equally valuable cycle. Track the alternative route actually available and the time remaining in the scoring window. Do not turn a rough hopper capacity into denied points. For a steal, distinguish fuel removed from an opponent’s reserve, fuel retained, fuel passed, fuel later scored and fuel lost back to the opponent. Avoid counting a transfer twice.

Leave unknown counts null. An empty event list means footage unreviewed, not that the match contained no relevant event. A camera cut creates a blind interval even if broadcast commentary continues. Multiple robots near a pile do not reveal their exact pickup share. Hub counts cannot generally assign individual scoring when streams overlap. Use the official score only at its actual alliance/phase resolution.

title: Geometry and failures need more than a plausible story
text:
## Geometry and failures need more than a plausible story

Record the deployed envelope as seen at the interaction: extension can change a trench-capable robot into a bump-only robot. When a defender constrains rotation, identify the bumper contact and nearby hub, trench bar, wall or bump separately. Do not infer exact clearance, mass, traction, moment of inertia or motor current from a camera image. A rounded perimeter changes the contact problem but cannot guarantee escape under every friction and obstacle condition.

For an operational interruption, mark the last unambiguous functioning action, the first abnormal action, any recovery, and which capabilities remain. “Collects but shoots short” differs from “entire robot dead.” A mechanism appearing damaged is not a diagnosis of root cause. Electrical logs, operator testimony or a technical publication may explain a symptom later; preserve the chronology and attribution of that new explanation. Do not label an unobserved problem a brownout because the score dropped.

source_locator.section: Geometry and failures need more than a plausible story

title: Reconcile with official components without inventing individual output
text:
## Reconcile with official components without inventing individual output

Keep final score, clean score, penalties received and each relevant official phase or component. Reconcile arithmetic and identify which alliance had each active shift. Own first/second active-shift totals in 2026 occur at different wall-clock times for opponents. The final-period fuel component is not climb output. The stored 2026 finals all record zero tower points for both alliances; fuel and access remain the useful questions in this series.

For 2026 match 3, official auto fuel is 188–118; post-auto fuel is 529–509; final is 717–632 because Milstein receives five penalty points. The commentator’s post-auto numbers are alliance quantities. For match 6, clean output is 678–691 and final is 688–691, with ten penalty points received by Milstein. A three-point final is not a three-point clean result. Preserve this distinction in quizzes and causal explanations.

In the upper-bracket final, Daly wins auto 186–83 and transition 65–30 but does not win every subsequent fuel component. In finals 2 it does lead every recorded fuel component, with the final period only 169–165. In finals 3 the own active-shift totals are 311–79, while final-period fuel is 154–161. Those patterns guide what footage to investigate; they cannot identify how many fuel a defender individually denied.

source_locator.section: Reconcile with official components without inventing individual output

title: Completion and verification
text:
## Completion and verification

Do not set complete=true until full interval coverage, all-six-robot follow checks, identity and clock alignment, camera blind spots, score reconciliation and explicit unresolved claims are present. It is acceptable for a completed viewing to leave a particular action unresolved because it is occluded. That uncertainty must remain visible; viewing completion is not omniscience. A user correction should identify the event/claim, the better source or timestamp, the revised interpretation and which downstream design conclusions need reconsideration.

The intended next step is playable match footage or an authorized usable video source. Until it exists, the six expanded 2026 narratives remain commentary evidence, and all eighty visual records remain pending. The JSONL ledger is the durable queue; it is not a certification of work that could not be performed.

title: 2023 published robot account · intake
text: ## 2023 published robot account · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A pasta-roller intake grips a cone flange and pinches a cube, constraining cones to tip-in or tip-out. A roller reorienter supplies the additional rotational degree of freedom needed for an upright handoff. Rollers are powered coaxially through the reorienter.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted ground pickup in arbitrary orientations; human-player throwing could shorten travel by an estimated 40% and reduce loading-zone traffic. Coaxial drive protects motors and reduces mass at the intake edge.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit strategy-to-mechanism chain: changing the pickup source reduces travel only if orientation and handoff remain reliable. The 40% is the team’s route estimate, not an independently measured cycle improvement. A broad capture envelope transfers complexity downstream unless the robot can reduce the resulting pose uncertainty. Compare full acquisition-to-scoring cycles, including difficult orientations, rather than pickup speed alone.

text: ## 2023 published robot account · transfer

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A linear intake slider brings the piece inward and permits frontal compliance. A separate horizontal scoring-arm slider reaches across the intake. A time-of-flight sensor first distinguishes orientation at a fixed location, then locates the piece laterally. The elevator lowers while the intake expels to hand off.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team needed handoff despite variable piece position across the intake width.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Do not collapse the two sliders into a single motion. The intake reduces some uncertainty, then sensing and the receiving mechanism handle what remains. This avoids requiring perfect passive centering, at the cost of coordinated motion, sensor interpretation and collision clearance. Sensor occlusion, flange shape, cone reflectivity and loaded mechanism deflection are plausible validation concerns, not failures established by this publication.

title: 2024 release and May 2025 follow-up · intake
text: ## 2024 release and May 2025 follow-up · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Polycarbonate rollers flex under impact; short dead-axle sections avoid a full-width shaft permanently bending. The team reports rollers deflecting more than half their diameter in bad hits. Deployment ties the two sides through chain and a cross shaft inside the frame.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compliance, weight and packaging drove the split-axle construction. The team explicitly reports axle-mount bolts shearing and deployment chain snapping, unresolved during the season.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A compliant roller is not the same as a robust entire intake. Moving deformation away from a long shaft can concentrate load in axle bolts or a mechanically coupled deployment system. This matters directly to 1833’s request for something beefy: copy the load path and its known limitations, not merely the visible material. The 2026 independently driven arms are a later response to the chain failure, not a configuration that existed throughout 2024.

title: The Flush in-season release · drivetrain
text: ## The Flush in-season release · drivetrain

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

29-inch square chassis with WCP X2i modules and a 5.9:1 drive ratio; the team optimized for roughly 18-foot average sprint distance. Protective panels isolate electronics from falling coral.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Stability at high reach and the expected travel distance drive the stated choices.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Optimize acceleration and usable travel under the expected route distribution, rather than unloaded top speed alone. A larger support polygon can help a reaching superstructure while increasing congestion exposure. The published dimensions and ratio are a configuration snapshot; they do not prove the same ratio is best for 1833 or a different game.

title: Validation still required

title: The Flush elevator and arm · scoring
text: ## The Flush elevator and arm · scoring

source_locator.section: The Flush elevator and arm · scoring

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Single-stage elevator uses 2x2 uprights, cross bracing and chain drive on both sides. The release gives two Kraken X60s, 3:1 and 28 inches of motion; stator limits increased from 40A to 80A. The arm is rigidly tied side-to-side and its gearbox shimmed; the team describes detuning and reducing the drive to one motor at 100A to avoid tipping.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Rigidity, low backlash and precise automated control are explicit priorities.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Motor count and theoretical joint acceleration cannot be separated from robot stability. Dual-sided chain drive addresses carriage twist, while a rigid camera mount helps relate vision measurements to mechanism geometry. Preserve the stated revisions and the release’s mixed original/final motor annotations; do not silently combine every number into one certified event configuration.

title: Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake
text: ## The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake

source_locator.section: The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A full-width 4mm corrugated-plastic funnel loads from three sides through separately powered rollers. The gripper has independently powered left/right rollers, four coral rollers and two algae rollers, plus an open top.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted tolerant loading, horizontal L1 packing and precise placement. The open top avoids reef entanglement and permits a shallower coral release angle.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A funnel can absorb human-player variability while the gripper controls the final release. Independent sides support a different L1 placement policy rather than merely increasing raw roller power. This is an architectural option for a station-fed role, not evidence that floor coral pickup was unnecessary for every alliance. Corrugated plastic stiffness, folding and clearances must be evaluated in the installed package.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: The Flush climb/funnel interface · endgame
text: ## The Flush climb/funnel interface · endgame

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The release describes a roughly 3.5-pound climber including motor and gearbox, stowed below the funnel, surgical-tubing extension and a 15:1 winch with a 2:1 pulley. A rear funnel ramp unfolds to clear the cage and climb.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compact packaging preserves the loading system while providing cage engagement tolerance.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The climb is coupled to the funnel’s motion and the loaded robot CG. A compact mechanism is not necessarily easy to approach under traffic; validate capture, retraction and failures with the actual funnel and piece state. These are team-reported design quantities, not measured masses or an exhaustive installed-version history.

title: The Flush and separate Quixshot offseason machine · controls
text: ## The Flush and separate Quixshot offseason machine · controls

source_locator.section: The Flush and separate Quixshot offseason machine · controls

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The Flush uses predictive target selection, smooth handover from driver motion, reef-clearance sequencing and separate local/global localization. The team reports 547/549 L2-L4 coral placements over its last two events. Quixshot is a distinct offseason coral launcher with manually tuned launch velocity differentials and a one-time intake deploy latch.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team reports that packaging a ground pickup with the in-season climber became difficult, so the compatible pickup was instead installed on the offseason launcher.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Do not attach Quixshot’s launcher to the in-season elevator robot. The 99.6% is a bounded team-reported placement statistic, not full-match reliability or 99.6% for every task. The published offseason answer says it did not deep-climb or handle algae at that point. The strongest transferable lesson is a deliberate interface and packaging trade, not the assertion that launching always beats placing.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Distinct offseason machine
text:
## Distinct offseason machine

Quixshot is a separate robot. The team’s July reply explains that a ground intake intended for the in-season machine conflicted with climber packaging and was installed on the launcher instead. Launch velocity differentials were manually tuned. The first offseason answer explicitly says no algae or deep climb at that point. Do not combine the two robots into one imaginary in-season architecture. Source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2025-offseason-robot-quixshot/504607/55

title: 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader
text:
# 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

title: Toploader DPC serializer · transfer
text: ## Toploader DPC serializer · transfer

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A rotating capture mechanism scoops fuel from a circular plywood bucket. Rotation and up-feed have separate motors; side rollers use omni wheels. Successive fuel pushes through a corrugated-plastic tube shaped by printed ends. The bucket separates into two sections for service.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team identified serialization as the limiting process and designed the robot around it. Independent drives allow software adjustment of rotation versus up-feed.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

The capture point moves to available fuel rather than relying solely on gravity bringing fuel to a stationary throat. Independent feed authority can help tune pile interaction and column delivery separately, but the release does not establish a universal motor-ratio setting. Bucket geometry, turret support and electronics access are part of the same flow system. Prototype rates of about 15 BPS single-stream and 23 BPS full-width are comparison claims, not sustained match scoring rates.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader chassis · drivetrain
text: ## Toploader chassis · drivetrain

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

A 27-inch square frame preserves circular bucket area without custom swerves or chamfered corners. Internal bars protect battery and module compartments; rear bumper mounts integrate armor for serializer protection.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Maximize the serializer’s available area with manufacturable hardware and protect internal mechanisms.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit packaging choice. It sacrifices some geometric freedom to keep the central circular feed volume useful with standard drive components. Frame perimeter, usable interior area and turret swept volume must be compared together. The team separately describes bump-only autonomous constraints; no unreviewed trench state or chassis specification should be inferred.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader inset turret · scoring
text: ## Toploader inset turret · scoring

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The turret is supported from above and packaged to reduce swept volume. Its sliding bearing stacks polycarbonate and aluminum plates; printed PETG spacers set clearance empirically and grease reduces friction.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Moving scoring and feeding were judged worth a lower single-stream ceiling; small swept volume preserves hopper capacity and flow.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

A turret changes more than aiming. Its supports and swept envelope can obstruct fuel entering the serializer, so a nominal capacity comparison that ignores the moving assembly is incomplete. This release supports a manufacturable impact-tolerant bearing concept, not exact dimensions, a universal bearing preload or independently verified shot accuracy. The team’s rate trade is tied to its intended moving role.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader independently deployed arms · intake
text: ## Toploader independently deployed arms · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Each intake arm uses an X44 deploy motor. Protected motors belt-drive compliant dead-axle polycarbonate rollers with silicone tubing and TPU pulley plugs. TPU belt supports retain the belts during deflection. A one-time kicker deploy uses surgical tubing and flexible plugs/string.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team explicitly connects independent deployment to eliminating the mechanically linked 2024 chain failure. Polycarbonate was preferred over SRPP to avoid permanent deformation changing belt centers.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Compliance must preserve transmission function, not just prevent fracture. A flexible arm changes belt geometry under load; supporting the belt during that motion is an integral part of the architecture. The team reports that TPU replaced brittle PETG roller plugs, with 100% infill and four-wall printing, and that wear still requires replacement every one or two events. Repairable consumables are not maintenance-free hardware.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake
text: ## Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Intake deployment extends a sliding hopper; surgical tubing retracts it. Two laminated layers of corrugated plastic provide stiffness. Slots are reinforced with 0.090-inch polycarbonate sandwiched between sheets; panels use tape and adhesive for replacement.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

The publication emphasizes low mass, robust sliding and easy manufacture/repair with limited router access.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

This is a specific example of an intake–storage interface, useful to 1833’s morph chart. Linking deployment reduces independent actuation but also links faults and operating states. Slot reinforcement addresses local bearing and deformation loads that a generic corrugated-plastic wall description misses. Capacity, deflection and passage access should be measured in each loaded state; no unverified hopper capacity is assigned here.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader readiness and localization · controls
text: ## Toploader readiness and localization · controls

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

Scoring requires launch velocity, launch angle and turret yaw within tolerance plus a recent image with at least two tags. The serializer pauses when readiness fails. PhotonVision MultiTag selects camera poses using hub/total tag visibility and rejects old or ambiguous poses.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

Single-driver operation reduces communication overhead; automated gating is intended to release fuel only from useful launch states.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Feed interruption is an intentional interface between aiming and serialization, not automatically a jam. A high mechanical BPS ceiling is useful only while readiness remains true. Logging the reason for each gating interruption would distinguish vision starvation, aim error and actual feed trouble. The release does not demonstrate those duty fractions or an electrical diagnosis of every stop.

title: Validation still required
text:
### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

title: Toploader partner-aware bump autonomous · controls
text: ## Toploader partner-aware bump autonomous · controls

title: Published construction or code
text:
### Published construction or code

The team describes timestamping partner paths, targeting leftover fuel after the trench race, using reusable path partials and adjustable pauses without redeployment. A Pac-Man routine is identified at NorCal DCMP playoff match 1.

title: Stated rationale and boundaries
text:
### Stated rationale and boundaries

A bump-only robot was expected to reach midfield later; route selection was built around shorter partners rather than competing for the same initial race.

title: Engineering interpretation
text:
### Engineering interpretation

Architectural limitations can become planning inputs instead of being hidden by an ideal autonomous animation. Preserve the team’s distinction between pre-Champs crossing rules and later rules, and between experiments and actually used routines. A clever path is not proof every prototype routine competed. The release does not establish a tower mechanism; absence from the selected technical sections remains unknown, not certified absence.

title: 1833’s supplied 2026 design workflow
text:
# 1833’s supplied 2026 design workflow

The original workbook and PDF are preserved under team1833/. Their statements are historical team planning, not validated game rules or independent mechanism measurements. Cell-level and PDF-page text exports permit exact retrieval. No source workbook or PDF was edited.

The workbook contains parallel group task lists, numeric priority/difficulty judgments, formulas multiplying those ordinal values, and a cleaned must/might/won’t list. Some sheets have inconsistent priority scales. The cleaned list’s repeated “No” final-decision cells must not be interpreted as rejecting every must-do task. Group 4 even distinguishes autonomous climb priority in qualifications versus eliminations. Keep group opinions and later decisions separate instead of silently averaging them into a consensus.

The PDF maps requirements into intake, storage, shooter, climb, electrical and chassis concepts. It records historical mechanism references, pros/cons and open prototype questions about compression and roller materials. It explicitly asks for service access, wire protection and mechanical/electrical compatibility. The shooter page contains proposed distances, angles and velocities; these are unverified calculations, with launch-height, drag and other assumptions needing reconstruction before reuse. References such as 2020 spindexer slot capacity must not become universal capacity limits for 2026 bulk serializers.

For the agent: reproduce the task-to-requirement-to-concept chain, preserve alternatives and open tests, and distinguish kickoff judgments from later evidence. The early climb priorities are historical inputs; the user’s later correction and tower-only data establish a fuel-first default for the studied 2026 competitive context. Do not overwrite the original documents to make hindsight look like the initial decision. A future task sheet should carry rule revision, phase, partner assumptions, expected contribution, ordinal priority meaning, development cost, evidence and decision rationale. A mechanism comparison should identify which requirement it serves and what observation would change the choice.

title: Required 1833 task sheet
text:
## Required 1833 task sheet

For each new game/manual analysis, material rules revision or new/revised robot design brief, fill a fresh copy of [the one-sheet template](../../team1833/1833_Task_List_Template.xlsx). Follow `docs/TASK_LIST_PROTOCOL.md` and `team1833/task_template_schema.json`, with all paths resolved from the corpus root. The template includes task outcome, phase, points/enabling value, priority, difficulty, recommendation, rationale, alliance dependencies, acceptance target, exact rule/source, uncertainty/test and separate human decision. No group tabs; no inherited season-specific decisions. Four previously blocked 604 image originals are now recovered and embedded (2023 robot; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper).

title: 1833 required task-list protocol
text: # 1833 required task-list protocol

title: Required deliverable and trigger
text:
## Required deliverable and trigger

For every new-season manual analysis, material rules revision, or new/revised robot design brief, fill a fresh copy of `team1833/1833_Task_List_Template.xlsx` before presenting the final architecture recommendation. The required output is a populated workbook with exactly one worksheet, `Task List`. Do not create group tabs. The blank canonical template must remain blank. Save the populated copy under a dated season-and-brief filename; preserve previous analyses so changed priorities can be explained. For a small revision, revise a copy of the previous sheet and identify the changed assumption or rule and its consequences in the rationale. The template is a work product requirement, not a guarantee that a model will obey without being given this protocol.

title: Establish the decision context
text:
## Establish the decision context

Fill the six metadata inputs C2:H7: season/game; exact manual revision and governing source URL; target event, week and competition stage; expected alliance roles and opponent assumptions; 1833's time, people, fabrication, budget, robot packaging, practice and maintenance constraints; and agent/date/human review status. Unknown inputs must be explicitly marked unknown with the assumption used provisionally. Historical EPA, alliance scores and Worlds examples do not substitute for the current manual or team constraints. If these are not available, produce a provisional sheet and identify the missing inputs rather than inventing them.

title: Enumerate the work before choosing mechanisms
text:
## Enumerate the work before choosing mechanisms

Use one actionable task or required outcome per row, beginning at row 13. Cover every legal task and enabling capability that could matter: mobility and traversal, acquisition, storage and transfer, resource control, scoring, autonomous, endgame, alignment/sensing, defense/support, and other legal actions. These are starter categories, not mandatory robot subsystems. Add or rename categories when the game requires it. Record an excluded or inapplicable task with the reason instead of silently omitting it. Split the same task into separate rows when autonomous/teleop, event stage, alliance role, field location or game state changes its value materially. Keep a functional task such as collecting floor pieces separate from an architecture proposal such as a slapdown intake; mechanisms are evaluated after the functional priorities are stated.

Columns A–N are defined in `team1833/task_template_schema.json` and in the worksheet header. For each occupied task row, complete A–F and H–M; G is calculated. Use N/A plus a reason where a field truly does not apply, and unknown plus a smallest decision-changing test where evidence is missing. Column N is reserved for an actual human decision/rationale: leave blank or label pending human review until 1833 supplies a decision. Never fabricate human approval. Preserve the user's explicit corrections as attributed context alongside their date and scope.

source_locator.section: Enumerate the work before choosing mechanisms

title: Give priorities a defensible meaning
text:
## Give priorities a defensible meaning

Priority 1 means essential to the proposed role; 2 means valuable; 3 means optional. Difficulty uses the team's relative Fibonacci scale: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. Explain the basis of both judgments in Why / tradeoff. Do not treat the product P×D as an objective ranking, a points-per-effort model or a decision rule. The supplied original workbook used priority times difficulty; this template retains that discussion aid without claiming it captures strategic value. A difficult must-do can remain a must-do. A high-point action can be unnecessary for this robot when an alliance partner covers it. Enabling tasks and denial can be valuable without directly scoring points.

Use the Agent recommendation dropdown: Must do, Might do, Won’t do, or Needs discussion. State the opportunity cost, partner dependency, game-state conditions and reliability assumptions that could change it. Column D should distinguish rule points from inferred enabling value; include timing, capacity, accuracy or probability conditions when quantified. Do not invent numeric precision when the data supports only a qualitative judgment.

title: Make each recommendation testable and traceable
text:
## Make each recommendation testable and traceable

Acceptance target / units must describe a measurable functional outcome under specified conditions, or explicitly say the target is not yet established. Examples include loaded collection success, release accuracy at a stated location, usable capacity with the mechanism swept envelope, sustained throughput including acquisition and readiness interruptions, or recovery time after a jam. These examples are not requirements or performed tests. Record the rule number/section/page and revision, and the exact source or corpus locator behind each factual claim. Clearly distinguish official rules, team-reported performance, attributed commentary, 1833's judgment and agent inference. Unknowns / smallest test should identify what observation or prototype result could change the priority or architecture.

After filling the sheet, compare at least two coherent architectures against the same prioritized tasks and constraints. Cite historical inspiration by year/team/version and inspect the whole acquisition-to-output interface. Feed architecture findings back into the sheet when they change difficulty, dependencies or acceptance criteria. Preserve both the initial reason and the reason for the revision. Do not jump from famous team names to compatibility claims.

title: Workbook handling and completion gate
text:
## Workbook handling and completion gate

The starter table `RobotTasks` occupies A12:N92, providing 80 task rows. It is a starting capacity, not a task limit. If more rows are needed, insert rows within/at the end of the table and extend the table, G formulas, E/F/H validations and summary ranges in B10/E10/H10/K10 to include every occupied row; move the provenance footer below the table. Do not add another worksheet. Keep frozen headings and task columns. G must remain blank until task, priority and difficulty are supplied. Summary counts count only the named statuses; verify no recommendation is left on an unused row and no placeholder category row is counted as a task.

Before delivering, check exactly one sheet, correct manual revision, all task categories considered, all occupied rows documented, no invented decisions, formulas recalculated, no spreadsheet errors, and source locators preserved. Unresolved items may remain explicitly unresolved; their existence must be reflected in the confidence and proposed tests. Deliver the filled workbook with the design analysis. A prose task list alone does not satisfy the user's requested workflow.

title: How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis
text:
A complete available-caption study of the upper-bracket final and all three 2026 Einstein finals. The central account is the coupling of autonomous contact, transition position, neutral-zone supply, steal timing, shoot-on-the-move passing and 4065’s defensive geometry. Breakdowns and uncertain intent remain explicit confounders.

Compare whole alliance control loops, not drum rate against turret rate in isolation. A robot can make a smaller immediate score while changing who owns the next supply of fuel, who can arrive before a shift starts and which opponent must cross a defended bottleneck. The source’s counterfactual wins and point-denial estimates are hypotheses, not measured individual contributions.

title: Upper bracket: 1323’s corner cut, a disrupted 2910 auto and the 4414–4065 follow route
text: The useful design requirement is an autonomous system whose acquisition envelope, collision recovery and route compatibility are evaluated together. A route can abandon a small pocket yet improve total possession by reaching a more valuable arc first. A high collection rate can create an exit-path problem if the loaded robot cannot traverse the selected obstacle without shedding fuel. A net is therefore part of the mobility–storage interface, not an isolated capacity feature. None of this gives a dimension, actual retained count or certified causal diagnosis of 2910’s auto error. Reproduce the route interaction with synchronized overhead video and logs before concluding that the same cut always defeats the same opponent.

title: Upper bracket first active shifts: dual moving passers clean supply while imposing incidental delay
text: This is a coupled acquisition, passing and interference role. Passing while moving can let an off-shift robot keep collecting instead of serializing collect, stop, orient and release; the same motion can close an opponent’s useful approach. That does not make every turret a good moving passer. Intake throughput, feed continuity, aiming under motion, range, loaded acceleration and the ability to keep fuel on the intended side all matter. Fuel temporarily held in a third robot is another supply state, even if that robot scores little. The source supplies neither a complete fuel ledger nor timing measurements, so avoid turning this account into a quantified claim that turrets always clean the field faster than drums.

title: Upper bracket: starvation changes departure location, which changes the next steal and partner release
text: Track location and inventory at every shift boundary. A robot with the same amount of fuel but a different terminal position can have a very different next assignment. Supply denial may first force a detour, then postpone a steal, then expose a partner’s prepared pile; simply counting immediate defended scoring seconds misses those downstream opportunities. The reported three-second gain remains an estimate from edited commentary. Alternative explanations include traffic, operator choice and recovery from previous contact. An auditable event log should separate observed departure, observed arrival, unknown fuel count and inferred causal link, rather than give one long causal sentence the status of a directly observed fact.

text: A hopper-full shooter rate is not the marginal match rate when the remaining fuel is dispersed. Distinguish release-limited, collection-limited and route-limited phases. A high-rate drum can still be strategically excellent if partners prepare dense piles or clear crossings; a moving turret can still be slow if each remaining pickup is difficult. The official upper-bracket data also limits the story: Daly leads auto 186–83 and transition 65–30, but Newton scores more in its second own active shift, 173–97, and the final period, 176–145. The source’s supply-control account should not be rewritten as Daly winning every phase. Each alliance’s own active-shift totals occur at different wall-clock periods.

title: How 254 beat their California counterparts at the World Championship! | FRC Strategy Analysis
text:
A complete available-caption study of 2026 Einstein match 3 (Curie–Milstein) and match 6 (Milstein–Johnson). The retrospective connects tall-dumper throughput to crossing risk, neutral-zone control, coordinated steals, 4946’s rounded perimeter and 6324’s flexible screening role. Its “lose auto by one” thesis is a conditional hypothesis, not a settled rule.

Architecture determines the set of routes available at a particular loaded configuration. Extended storage can turn a trench-capable robot into a bump-only robot during the exact interval when a steal requires escape. A partner that clears a crossing can be worth more than another marginal load, but the value depends on current inventory, shift timing and the defender’s recovery. Test these interactions as an alliance system.

It is not a proof that a rounded robot always has leverage or that polygons are always trapped. The pick reversal is a driver-training insight: a good defender needs escape practice as well as pursuit practice.
